text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA

- Yugoslav delegation, headed by finance minister Tomica Raicevic, returns today from from talks with the IMF in Washington where it handed over legal documents necessary for the normalisation of membership in the institution.
- Independent metal workers' trade union Nezavisnost decides to launch on Sept 9 a wave of strikes and protests asking the government to find work for the metal industry.
- President of the Serbian trade union association Tomislav Banovic calls for electricity prices to be returned to July levels.
- Pribojska banka AD was closed down. The bank was 20 million dinars in the red.
- Serbia's taxi drivers will go on strike on September 9 if their demands to adjust taxes with their earnings are not met.
POLITKA
- Yugoslav Supreme defence council holds session, makes new appointments and examines current military-political sitaution in the region.
- Belgrade will host the third conference of southeastern European capitals in September 1997, it was decided at the second conference in Vienna.
- Yugoslav delegation ends fourth round of talks on succession in Brussels, announces possible meeting of all countries emerging from the former Yugoslavia in October.
- Yugoslav-Italian talks on trans-Balkan gas pipeline end in Milocer. The pipeline to go from Dimitrovgrad via Nis, Podgorica and Bar to Brindisi.
- Yugoslav Agriculture Minister Tihomir Vrebalov in talks with oil producers announces new sunflower price to be from 1.80 to two dinars per kilo.
- Normalisation of transport with foremr Yugoslav republics possible in a very short period but solid inter-state agreements are needed, the Yugoslav chamber of economy says.
- Ruling Socialist Party of Serbia holds its first election convention in Center Sava.
- Kragujevac mayor Zivorad Nesic and president of Zastava group Srboljub Vasovic call workers of Zastava arms to return to work.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Normalisation of relations with countries in the territory of the former Yugoslavia help incerease work of our firms and extend markets, says director general of Grmec.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Banja Luka, in Bosnian Serb republic, to hold first international book fair from September 17 to 22.
